claim.quote: A lower bound of 114.4 GeV/c2 is established, at the 95% confidence level, on the mass of the Standard Model Higgs boson.

key_value.quote: A lower bound of 114.4 GeV/c2 is established, at the 95% confidence level, on the mass of the Standard Model Higgs boson.

key_value_text.quote: A lower bound of 114.4 GeV/c2 is established, at the 95% confidence level, on the mass of the Standard Model Higgs boson.
key_value_text.value: Combined LEP2 direct-search data exclude a Standard Model Higgs boson lighter than 114.4 GeV/c^2 at 95% confidence level.

name: Search for the Standard Model Higgs Boson at LEP

summary.plain: LEP never found the Higgs boson, but by not finding it, the four experiments together proved it had to be heavier than 114.4 GeV - a limit that guided the search for years afterward.
summary.technical: ALEPH, DELPHI, L3, OPAL and LEP Higgs Working Group combination, Phys. Lett. B 565 (2003) 61-75 (arXiv:hep-ex/0306033); a lower bound of 114.4 GeV/c^2 at 95% confidence level on the Standard Model Higgs boson mass, from the combined LEP2 direct-search data.

title: Search for the Standard Model Higgs Boson at LEP
why_it_matters: Set the strongest lower bound on the Higgs boson mass before the LHC era, ruling out a large swath of parameter space and shaping the design and early-run strategy of the LHC's own Higgs search.
